newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stock index struggles to new closing high.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stock index struggles to new closing high.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index struggled to a new closing high on Wednesday, but the overall market was mixed as weak gold prices offset the impact of falling Canadian interest rates.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 0.40 points to a record close of 5481.00, barely surpassing Tuesday's all-time high.
Trading was heavy with 103.9 million shares exchanging hands worth C$1.56 billion ($1.15 billion).
But declining stocks outnumbered advances 503 to 426 with 289 issues unchanged.
"It probably can be attributed to the gold stocks," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman with Maison Placements Canada Inc.
Gold and precious metal stocks were depressed by weaker Comex gold prices. Transportation and communication issues also were among the seven sub-groups which ended lower.
The TSE's seven strong sectors were led by financial services, retailing and pipelines.

The financial services group rose after the Bank of Canada dropped its key bank rate by a quarter point to 3.75 percent, prompting the big banks to cut their prime lending rates a quarter point to 5.25 percent.
The central bank's move was anticipated after economic data released last week showed the Canadian economy remains sluggish.
But some investors are concerned that the economy will take a serious hit from the ongoing General Motors Corp. strike in Canada which began Oct. 2, Bradley said.
Market players were also disappointed that Prime Minister Jean Chretien ruled out an across-the-board tax cut in a speech Tuesday night.
Bradley noted that the interest rate reductions will spur home construction, but other areas of consumer spending remain sluggish due to stagnant personal incomes.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. fell 2 to 20.95 on 12.3 million shares as questions grew about the company's ownership of a huge gold discovery in Indonesia.

* Bank of Montreal gained 0.40 to 40.30 on 2.5 million shares after announcing plans for a continent-wide virtual bank subsidiary. Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce eased 0.15 to 55, while Royal Bank of Canada climbed 0.40 to 42.45.
* Wharf Resources Ltd. rose 1.30 to 9.20 after Goldcorp Inc offered C$86 million ($63 million) for the rest of Wharf it does not own.

* Some oil stocks were also heavy traders. Stampeder Exploration Ltd. edged up 0.05 to 6.40 on 1.7 million shares after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 6.65. Arbitragers are continued to settle accounts following Stampeder's takeover of Morgan Hydrocarbons Inc.
Talisman Energy Inc. climbed 0.55 to 39.95 on 1.6 million shares on stronger oil prices and a bright production forecast. The stock earlier hit a 52-week peak of 40. earlier
